examples.question_text:
Determine whether each function is a valid probability density function, taking $f(x)=0$ outside the stated interval.
(a) $f(x)=\dfrac{3x^2}{27}$ on $[0,3]$.
(b) $f(x)=\dfrac{x}{10}$ on $[0,4]$.
(c) $f(x)=\dfrac{3}{32}(x^2-8x+12)$ on $[0,8]$.
examples.solution_text:
(a) $f(x)\ge0$ throughout $[0,3]$.
$\begin{align*}\int_0^3\frac{3x^2}{27}\,dx&=\left[\frac{x^3}{27}\right]_0^3\\&=1\end{align*}$
Both conditions hold, so this is a valid PDF.

(b) $f(x)\ge0$ throughout $[0,4]$.
$\begin{align*}\int_0^4\frac{x}{10}\,dx&=\left[\frac{x^2}{20}\right]_0^4\\&=\frac45\end{align*}$
The integral is not $1$, so this is not a valid PDF.

(c) $f(x)=\dfrac{3}{32}(x-2)(x-6)$ is negative when $2<x<6$.
$\begin{align*}\int_0^8\frac{3}{32}(x^2-8x+12)\,dx&=\frac{3}{32}\left[\frac{x^3}{3}-4x^2+12x\right]_0^8\\&=\frac{3}{32}\left(\frac{512}{3}-256+96\right)\\&=1\end{align*}$
Although the integral is $1$, the function is negative on part of its domain, so it is not a valid PDF.

examples.question_text:
A probability density function $f(x)$ is zero outside $[4,10]$. Write an integral for each probability and state the value in (d).
(a) $P(X\le7)$.
(b) $P(2\le X\le8)$.
(c) $P(X\ge6)$.
(d) $P(X\ge1)$.
examples.solution_text:
The density is zero below $4$ and above $10$, so restrict the integration limits to its support.

(a) $P(X\le7)=\displaystyle\int_4^7 f(x)\,dx$.

(b) $P(2\le X\le8)=\displaystyle\int_4^8 f(x)\,dx$.

(c) $P(X\ge6)=\displaystyle\int_6^{10} f(x)\,dx$.

(d) $P(X\ge1)=\displaystyle\int_4^{10} f(x)\,dx=1$, since this includes the whole support.

examples.question_text: A continuous random variable has PDF $f(x)=\dfrac{3x^2}{215}$ on $[1,6]$, and $0$ elsewhere. Find $P(2<X<5)$.
A continuous random variable has PDF $f(x)=\dfrac{3}{2x^2}$ on $[1,3]$, and $0$ elsewhere. Find $P(X\ge2)$.
examples.solution_text:
The density is zero above $3$, so the upper integration limit is $3$.
$\begin{align*}P(X\ge2)&=\int_2^3\frac{3}{2}x^{-2}\,dx\\&=\frac32\left[-\frac1x\right]_2^3\\&=\frac32\left(-\frac13+\frac12\right)\\&=\frac14\end{align*}$

examples.question_text: A continuous random variable has PDF $f(x)=\dfrac{x}{18}$ on $[0,6]$, and $0$ elsewhere. Find $c$ such that $P(X\le c)=\dfrac49$.

examples.derivation: (a) The density is non-negative and its integral is [x^3/27]_0^3 = 1. (b) The density is non-negative but its integral is [x^2/20]_0^4 = 4/5. (c) Factoring gives 3(x−2)(x−6)/32, negative on (2,6); its integral is (3/32)(512/3−256+96) = 1. The three conclusions correctly apply both PDF conditions.
Intersecting each requested region with [4,10] gives integration intervals [4,7], [4,8], [6,10] and [4,10], respectively. The last includes the whole support and therefore has probability 1.

The density is non-negative and normalises to (6^3−1^3)/215 = 1. Integrating over (2,5) gives (5^3−2^3)/215 = 117/215. The diagram plots the same density on [1,6] and shades precisely the region from 2 to 5. Endpoint inclusion does not change the probability.
Normalisation gives (3/2)(1−1/3) = 1. The upper tail integrates from 2 to 3: (3/2)[−1/x]_2^3 = (3/2)(1/2−1/3) = 1/4.
The density normalises to [x^2/36]_0^6 = 1. Setting c^2/36 = 4/9 gives c^2 = 16. Only c = 4 lies in [0,6], so rejecting −4 is correct.
